Meet Sandown School’s Governing Board
Find out about the school’s governors and the work that we do.
Our commitment: to ensure that all at Sandown reach its aspiration of being: ‘The best that we can be’.

Our organisation and working structure:-
Our Governing Board operates through a ‘circle’ structure. It is dynamic, efficient and an effective way of working. We meet and work as a whole governing board across the school year.
Our meetings are at school in the late afternoon and last around two hours. We attend training sessions and seminars. These help us keep up to date with changes in schools and education and to help us do our job effectively.
Individual governors are linked to particular areas of school life. We regularly visit the school and liaise with staff and meet with pupils. This helps us find out how the school is progressing towards its targets. Welcome to Reception - Oak and Maple classes
Miss Richford and Mrs Cooper would like to welcome all children and their families to Sandown School.
We acknowledge that starting school can be an exciting but also an anxious time for both children and their parents and carers. Therefore, we work hard to ensure that all families have a smooth transition from Nursery into Reception. We begin this in July with communication with nurseries, home visits, Teddy Bears Picnics and inviting all parents and carers to Class Dojo. When the school year begins in September, we focus on the children being happy and settled above all. We truly believe that happy, settled children become motivated, independent learners.
We are also very lucky to have two Nurture Teaching Assistants, who run Sandown Seagulls, Mrs Groves and Miss Blackman and a Speech and Language Teaching Assistant, who works closely with the children.
Terms 1 & 2
What a fantastic start to Reception! The children have settled in well to their first term at school. We have done a lot of exciting things this term! The children have begun their phonics journey and are enjoying learning lots of new sounds. They have also been learning to read and represent numbers. In the Let’s Explore project, the children explored their classroom and school grounds to help them feel settled and happy in their new surroundings. We also learnt about the local environment and found out about places the children have visited on holiday. The children enjoyed looking at and creating maps for journeys. We ended the term with a trip to explore our local area.
Our journey ended at Christ Church Ore, where we met Rachel, who told us about the church and why it is a special place for Christians. Thank you to all the parents for their support in their child’s first term at school.
This term in Reception, we have been learning about technology, how it is part of our daily lives and how machines can help us. We started the term making smoothies using a blender and explored other machines that make our lives easier, such as hoovers, calculators, telephones, and robots. The children built their own circuits and had the opportunity to tinker with the inside of some machines. To consolidate the learning, we designed, built and created our own marvellous machines, which we showcased to the other Reception class at our Marvellous Invention Convention. We had a very exciting visit from the local fire service exploring their fire engine, uniform and equipment. We ended the term with a visit from Father Christmas, a Christmas dinner and our spectacular nativity performance of ‘The Twinkly Nativity’. We certainly have some stars in the making.
Terms 3 & 4
This term, we have been exploring the topic ‘Long Ago’. We began the term by taking an adventure to the Sandown Museum, where we looked at objects from long ago and compared them to the ones we use today.
As well as looking at how objects and places have changed over time, we also looked at how the children have changed from babies to now and how they will change in the future. We were lucky enough to have a visit from a mother and their baby, where we learnt more about what babies can do and how they change as they grow. During the term, we looked at old toys and discussed how people used to make their own toys, food and clothes. We even made our own peg dolls.
At the end of the term, we invited our grandparents into school. We asked them a lot of questions, and they talked to us about what life was like for them as children and in school. They also taught us how to play some traditional games.
This term we have been learning about food and farming by exploring where food comes from, what plants and animals need to grow and how to keep ourselves healthy. We started the term with an adventure to The Hastings Country Park, where we went on a walk to see and learn about the food sources in the area and where they come from.
Throughout the term, we have been creating our own pictures of plants, fruits, vegetables and animals, thinking carefully about which parts are required.
We have enjoyed trying new foods and preparing food to eat, following instructions and recipes. We have made a fruit salad and butter.
We have been exploring our Sandown gardens with Kathryn, our school gardener, looking at spring flowers, planting bean seeds, strawberry plants, and potatoes, and cutting off the tops of root vegetables to grow the scraps.
We also celebrated World Book Day and Science Week this term. On World Book Day, we dressed up as our favourite book characters, got ready for a story, and spent the day sharing lots of books, creating our own Elmer the elephant, and recommending books for others to read.
The focus for Science Week this year was ‘Curiosity: What’s Your Question?’. Over the week, we became curious by asking questions as we explored bubbles and growing seeds in different temperatures and conditions. We also enjoyed a visit from Nicole from Glow Inspire, where we were immersed in stories through Science. At the end of the week, we went to a STEM-related Career Café.
At the end of the term, our parents joined us to find out what we had been learning and to plant sunflower seeds to take home and take care of.
Terms 5 & 6
Term 5
This term, Reception went on an ‘Animal Safari’. We started the term by learning how to care for pets and what all animals need to grow, survive and stay happy and healthy. The children also loved talking about their own pets and discovering signs of animals in the school grounds such as badgers, moles and foxes. We even found a hatched pigeon egg!
The children learned about animal features and practised sketching them, remembering to include all their features. We explored which animals had scales, fur or feathers and the types of habitats that these animals live in.
David Attenborough day was a huge success as we celebrated his 100th Birthday by dressing up as animals. Explorers, scientists or even David himself. The children learnt lots of facts about his life, watched parts of his documentaries, helped plant a wild flower garden and created their own animal masks.
We found out about various animal habitats, even creating our own in the woods, and compared the animals that live across the globe with animals that live here in the UK.
In Maths this term, we built on our subitising, counting and comparison skills and started using rekenreks.
Term 6 – On The Beach
WOW! What an exciting and busy end to the year we have had in Reception! Our topic this term was all about the seashore, the seas and oceans and how to protect them as well as staying safe at the beach. We began the term by exploring plants and creatures that live on the beach before discovering what lives in the shore and beyond. We also spent some time investigating the best materials to keep sailors safe and we loved doing some boatbuilding.
Later in the term, we discovered who works at the beach and how they keep us safe. We even went on a morning trip to Hastings Beach where we did a scavenger hunt and visited the RNLI boating station.
Sports Day was a great success and the children loved demonstrating their speed, balance and coordination whilst working in a team and were very proud of their achievements.

EYFS overview
EYFS intent
Through the Prime Areas, Sandown Early years grows independent, lifelong learners within a language rich environment.
Our Aims
At Sandown Primary School and Nursery our aim is to provide a secure environment where our children can feel safe to explore rich and diverse learning and developmental opportunities. In partnership with our families, we aim to build on previous learning and respond to children’s individual needs. We provide a sound basis for lifelong learning, enabling the children to begin the process of becoming independent, confident, active learners for life. We aim to provide teaching and learning experiences, indoors and outdoors, of the highest quality to help our children progress and be ready for their next stage of learning.
The Early Years Foundation Stage
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) applies to children from birth to the end of the Reception year. In our school, children can join the Early Years Foundation Stage from two years of age, starting in our Nursery Acorn group. Children who are 3 and 4 have the opportunity, when ready, to enter the Nursery Sapling group in preparation for starting school.
At Sandown we are committed to following the EYFS Framework; supporting our children to learn and develop in the seven inter-connected areas of learning:-
At Sandown, we see the Prime Areas as being fundamental building blocks for igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning, forming relationships and thriving. We also support our children in four specific areas, through which the three prime areas are strengthened and applied.
In each of these seven areas, there are Early Learning Goals (ELG’s) that define the expectations for most children to reach by the end of Reception.
The EYFS also includes the characteristics of effective teaching and learning. They highlight the importance of a child’s attitude to learning and their ability to play, explore and think critically about the world around them.
